'''Friedrich Hermann Schottky''' (24 July 1851 – 12 August 1935) was a German [[mathematician]] who worked on [[elliptic function|elliptic]], [[abelian function|abelian]], and [[theta function]]s and introduced [[Schottky group]]s and [[Schottky's theorem]].<ref name=":0">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Schottky}}</ref><ref>{{citation|author=Gavril Farkas|author-link=Gavril Farkas|year=2012|chapter=Prym varieties and their moduli|editor=Piotr Pragacz|title=Contributions to Algebraic Geometry|publisher=EMS Press|doi=10.4171/114-1/8|arxiv=1104.2886}}</ref>

==Biography==

Friedrich Hermann Schottky was born in [[Breslau]], [[Germany]] (now Wrocław, [[Poland]]). His father, Dr. Hermann Friedrich Schottky, was an English teacher and his mother, Louise Winkler, was a florist. He attended {{ill|Maria-Magdalenen-Gymnasium|de|Maria-Magdalenen-Gymnasium}} from 1860 to 1870, where his classmates included {{ill|Max Grube|de|Max Grube}}, {{ill|Heinrich Rosin|de|Heinrich Rosin}}, and [[Eberhard Gothein]].<ref>{{ill|Marie Luise Gothein|de|Marie Luise Gothein}}: [http://s2w.hbz-nrw.de/ulbbn/content/titleinfo/972686 ''Eberhard Gothein. Ein Lebensbild. Seinen Briefen nacherzählt.''] Kohlhammer, Stuttgart 1931.</ref> From 1870 to 1874 he attended the [[University of Breslau]].<ref name=":0"/>

In 1875 Schottky received his doctorate, studying under 
[[Karl Weierstrass]] and [[Hermann von Helmholtz]] at [[Friedrich Wilhelm University of Berlin]].<ref>{{citation | author=Bölling, R. | year=1998 | chapter=Weierstrass and some members of his circle: Kovalevskaia, Fuchs, Schwarz, Schottky. | editor1=Begehr, H. | editor2= Koch, H. | editor3=Kramer, J. | editor4=Schappacher, N. | editor5=Thiele, E.J. | title=Mathematics in Berlin |publisher=Birkhäuser | location=Basel |doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8787-8_9}}</ref>

Schottky was a lecturer at the [[University of Breslau]] from 1878 to 1882, a professor at the [[University of Zurich]] from 1882 to 1892, and a professor at [[Philipps University of Marburg]] from 1892 to 1902. In 1902, through his friendship with [[Ferdinand Georg Frobenius]], Schottky was able to obtain a professorship at [[Friedrich Wilhelm University of Berlin]] where he would remain until his retirement in 1922.<ref>{{cite book| author=Thomas Hawkins | author-link=Thomas W. Hawkins Jr.
| title=The Mathematics of Frobenius in Context: A Journey Through 18th to 20th Century Mathematics | year=2013 |publisher=Springer}}</ref>

Schottky was elected to the Berlin Academy of Sciences in 1903.<ref>{{citation|date=20 February 1903| title=Scientific Notes and News| journal=Science| volume=17| number=425| doi=10.1126/science.17.425.317| url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.17.425.317| url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Schottky died in [[Berlin]] in 1935.<ref name=":0"/>

Schottky married Henriette Schottky (née Hammer, 1858–1947) and had 5 children, including the physicist [[Walter H. Schottky]] and the botanist [[Ernst Max Schottky]].<ref name=":0" />

==Mathematics==

Schottky's thesis on [[conformal mapping]] was well regarded by Weierstrass. Published in journal form in 1877, it introduced [[automorphic functions]] and [[Schottky groups]], to be developed several years later by [[Henri Poincaré]] and [[Felix Klein]].{{sfn|Schottky|1877}}<ref name=":0"/><!--{{sfn|Bolling|1998}}-->

Schottky's 1887 paper contributed to the theory of [[Poincaré series (modular form)|Poincaré series]].{{sfn|Schottky|1887}}

In [[algebraic geometry]], the problem of characterizing when the [[abelian varieties]] of an algebraic curve are [[Jacobian varieties]] is called the [[Schottky problem]]. Initially posed by [[Bernhard Riemann]], Schottky obtained the first results, for the case of genus 4,{{sfn|Schottky|1888}} and made subsequent progress with his student [[Heinrich Jung]].{{sfn|Schottky|Jung|1909}} The problem was formally solved in 1986 by [[Takahiro Shiota]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=Shiota |first=Takahiro |year=1986 |title=Characterization of Jacobian varieties in terms of soliton equations |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=83 |issue=2 |pages=333–382 |doi=10.1007/BF01388967}}</ref> but remains an area of active research.<ref>{{citation|last=Grushevsky|first=Samuel|chapter=The Schottky Problem |editor1-last=Caporaso |editor1-first=Lucia |editor1-link=Lucia Caporaso | editor2-last=McKernan | editor2-first=James |editor2-link=James McKernan |editor3-last=Popa |editor3-first=Mihnea |editor3-link=Mihnea Popa |editor4-last=Mustata | editor4-first=Mircea |editor4-link=Mircea Mustață
 |title=Current Developments in Algebraic Geometry |series=MSRI Publications |year=2011 | volume= 59 |arxiv=1009.0369}}</ref>

In [[complex analysis]], [[Schottky's theorem]] shows the existence of a bound on the value a holomorphic function can take on the unit disk.{{sfn|Schottky|1904}}

== Publications ==
Schottky authored 55 papers and one book.<ref name=":0"/>
